mechanism: Mefloquine is neurotoxic and can cause neuropsychiatric effects and peripheral neuropathy; alpha lipoic acid has antioxidant properties that may theoretically offer neuroprotection but lacks sufficient evidence to reliably mitigate mefloquine-induced neurotoxicity.
action: Monitor for signs of mefloquine neurotoxicity (dizziness, ataxia, peripheral neuropathy, psychiatric symptoms); alpha lipoic acid may be considered as adjunctive neuroprotection but should not be relied upon as primary mitigation.
